p: am/is/are + -ing for something happening now or around now, not finished yet.
Also for changes in progress: getting better, rising, starting to …
e: Shh, the baby is sleeping.
Prices are going up every month.
1.ru: Действие происходит сейчас или в этот период и ещё не закончено.

p: Present simple (work / works) for habits, routines, facts and things that are generally true.
Questions and negatives use do / does + base verb. Some verbs perform an action just by saying them: I promise, I apologise.
e: My brother works in a hotel.
Does the museum open on Mondays?
2.ru: Привычки, факты и то, что верно всегда; вопросы и отрицания — с do/does.

p: Continuous = temporary, happening now. Simple = permanent, repeated, in general.
always + continuous = something happens too often and is annoying.
e: I'm drinking tea today, but I usually drink coffee.
You're always losing your keys!
3.ru: Continuous — временно и сейчас; simple — обычно и всегда. always + -ing — раздражающая привычка.

p: State verbs (know, like, want, need, believe, belong, mean, seem…) are not usually continuous.
think, see, have, taste can be continuous when they mean an action (I'm thinking about it). He's being rude = behaving rudely now.
e: I need a new laptop. (not I'm needing)
We're thinking of moving.
4.ru: Глаголы состояния обычно не ставятся в continuous; исключения — когда они означают действие.

p: Past simple for finished actions at a finished time in the past.
Regular verbs add -ed; many verbs are irregular. Questions and negatives: did / didn't + base verb.
e: We went to Prague last spring.
I didn't see you at the party.
5.ru: Законченное действие в прошлом; вопросы и отрицания через did.

p: was/were + -ing for an action in progress at a past moment (the background).
A shorter past simple action often interrupts it: while I was cooking, the phone rang.
e: At 9 pm I was reading.
It started to rain while we were walking home.
6.ru: Длительное действие в момент прошлого; короткое действие в past simple его прерывает.

p: have/has + past participle connects the past with now: a result we can see now.
just, already, yet often go with it. gone = is there now; been = went and came back.
e: I've lost my keys, so I can't get in.
Have you finished yet?
7.ru: Прошлое действие с результатом в настоящем; just, already, yet.

p: Present perfect for experiences in your life up to now: Have you ever …? I've never …
Also with unfinished time: today, this week, so far. After It's the first time … use the present perfect.
e: Have you ever eaten sushi?
It's the first time I've flown.
8.ru: Опыт в жизни и незаконченный период; «впервые» — тоже present perfect.

p: have/has been + -ing for an activity that started in the past and has been going on until now (or just stopped).
We often say how long: for two hours, since Monday. It explains a present result: Why are you wet? I've been running.
e: It's been raining all day.
How long have you been waiting?
9.ru: Действие длится с прошлого до сейчас; акцент на процессе и длительности.

p: Continuous (have been doing) = the activity, how long. Simple (have done) = the finished result, how much / how many.
State verbs like know, have (own), belong use the simple form.
e: I've been writing emails all morning.
I've written ten emails.
10.ru: Процесс и длительность — continuous; результат и количество — simple.

p: To say how long something has lasted until now, use the present perfect (simple or continuous), not the present.
Use the simple form with state verbs: I've known her for years.
e: We've lived here since 2018.
How long have you been learning English?
11.ru: «Как долго до сих пор» — present perfect, а не настоящее время.

p: for + a period (for three days). since + the starting point (since Monday, since 2010).
When …? and ago take the past simple. It's (two years) since I last …
e: She's worked here for three months.
It's a year since I went to the cinema.
12.ru: for — сколько времени, since — с какого момента; ago и When — с past simple.

p: Present perfect: result now / connected to now. Past simple: finished, the time is over or clear.
Famous dead people and historical events use the past simple.
e: Tom has gone out. (he's not here now)
Tom went out ten minutes ago.
13.ru: Связь с настоящим — present perfect; законченное прошлое — past simple.

p: Finished time words (yesterday, last week, in 2010, ago) → past simple.
Unfinished time (today, this week, ever, so far, recently) → present perfect.
e: I saw Jane yesterday.
I haven't seen Jane today.
14.ru: Слова законченного времени — past simple, незаконченного — present perfect.

p: had + past participle for something that happened before another past moment.
Typical with when, by the time, already, before.
e: When we got to the station, the train had left.
I didn't go because I'd seen the film.
15.ru: Действие, случившееся раньше другого прошлого момента.

p: had been + -ing for an activity that continued up to a moment in the past.
It often explains a past situation: She was tired because she'd been working all day.
e: His clothes were wet. He'd been walking in the rain.
We'd been driving for hours when we stopped.
16.ru: Длительное действие, продолжавшееся до момента в прошлом.

p: have got = have for possession (mainly British, not for actions). Questions: Have you got …? / Do you have …?
have for actions (have breakfast, have a shower, have fun) can be continuous and uses do/did.
e: She's got two brothers.
Sorry, I'm having lunch.
17.ru: have got — владение; have как действие (завтракать, принимать душ) — может быть в continuous.

p: used to + verb for past habits or states that are not true now.
Negative and question: didn't use to / Did you use to …?
e: I used to live in a tiny flat.
Did you use to play football?
18.ru: Раньше было так, а сейчас нет.

p: Present continuous for future arrangements (plans with other people, already fixed).
Present simple for timetables and schedules (trains, films, terms).
e: I'm meeting Max on Friday.
The train leaves at 7.45.

p: going to + verb for plans you've already decided, and predictions from what you can see now.
was/were going to = a plan in the past that didn't happen.
e: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
I was going to call you, but my phone died.
20.ru: Намерение или прогноз по видимым признакам; was going to — несостоявшийся план.

p: will ('ll) for decisions made at the moment of speaking, offers, promises and refusals.
Shall I / Shall we …? for offers and suggestions.
e: It's cold. I'll close the window.
Shall we go for a walk?
21.ru: Решение в момент речи, предложение, обещание; Shall I/we — предложить.

p: will for predictions about the future, often with I think, I expect, probably, I'm sure.
Don't use will for arrangements already made (use the present continuous).
e: I think it'll rain later.
She probably won't come.
22.ru: Прогноз о будущем: I think, probably, I'm sure + will.

p: will = deciding now. going to = already decided.
going to also for predictions based on present evidence.
e: We've run out of bread. I'll buy some.
I'm going to paint the fence this weekend.
23.ru: will — решаю сейчас; going to — уже решил(а).

p: will be + -ing = in the middle of an activity at a future time.
will have + past participle = finished before a future time (by then, by Friday).
e: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Rome.
By 6 pm I'll have finished.
24.ru: will be doing — в процессе в будущем; will have done — завершится к моменту.

p: After when, if, as soon as, until, before, after — use the present (not will) for the future.
when = sure to happen; if = maybe.
e: I'll call you when I get home.
If it rains, we'll stay in.
25.ru: После when/if/until — настоящее время вместо will.

p: can / could for ability. be able to for other forms (will be able to, have been able to).
For one success in the past use was able to / managed to, not could.
e: I could swim when I was four.
The exit was blocked, but we managed to escape.
26.ru: Умение — can/could; разовый успех в прошлом — was able to / managed to.

p: could = it's possible, or a suggestion (We could go to the beach).
could have done = it was possible but didn't happen.
e: Don't climb that. You could fall.
You could have called me!
27.ru: could — возможность/предложение; could have done — могло быть, но не случилось.

p: must = I'm sure it's true. can't = I'm sure it's not true.
For the past: must have done / can't have done.
e: She's been working all day. She must be tired.
He didn't say hello. He can't have seen me.
28.ru: Уверенный вывод: must — точно да, can't — точно нет.

p: may / might = perhaps (it's possible). Negative: may not / might not.
For the past: may/might have done.
e: She might be at the gym.
They may have missed the bus.
29.ru: Возможно: may/might; о прошлом — may/might have done.

p: may / might for possible future actions or events.
might as well = there's no better option, so let's do it.
e: I might go to the concert.
The bus isn't coming. We might as well walk.
30.ru: Возможное будущее; might as well — «уж лучше / можно и».

p: have to = it's necessary (often a rule or a fact). must = often your own opinion or feeling.
For the past and future use had to / will have to. don't have to = it's not necessary.
e: I have to wear a uniform at work.
I must call Mum. It's been ages.
31.ru: have to — необходимость по правилам; must — личное мнение; don't have to — не обязательно.

p: mustn't = don't do it, it's wrong. don't need to / needn't = it's not necessary.
needn't have done = you did it, but it wasn't necessary.
e: You mustn't tell anyone.
You needn't bring food. There's plenty.
32.ru: mustn't — нельзя; needn't — не нужно; needn't have done — сделал(а) зря.

p: should / shouldn't to give advice or say what is right.
should have done = it was the right thing, but you didn't do it (regret, criticism).
e: You should go to the dentist.
I should have studied harder.
33.ru: Совет — should; упрёк о прошлом — should have done.

p: After insist, suggest, recommend, it's important/essential that … you can use should + verb or just the base verb.
suggest + -ing or suggest that + subject + verb (not suggest to do).
e: The doctor recommended that she rest.
She suggested going to the cinema.
34.ru: После suggest/insist/important that — should + глагол или просто глагол; suggest + -ing.

p: had better ('d better) + verb = strong advice for a specific situation now (or something bad will happen).
It's time + subject + past simple (It's time we went); It's time to + verb.
e: You'd better take an umbrella.
It's late. It's time we went home.
35.ru: 'd better — настоятельный совет сейчас; It's time we + прошедшее.

p: would for imaginary situations (I'd love a dog …).
would for repeated actions in the past, and wouldn't for refusals; I wish … would to complain.
e: It would be nice to live by the sea.
I wish you would stop interrupting!
36.ru: Воображаемое, привычки в прошлом, отказ (wouldn't), I wish … would — жалоба.

p: Can/Could you …? to ask someone to do something. Can/Could/May I …? to ask for permission.
Would you like …? to offer or invite; Would you mind + -ing? for polite requests.
e: Could you pass the salt, please?
Would you mind opening the window?
37.ru: Вежливые просьбы, разрешение, предложения и приглашения.

p: if + present … will = a real possibility.
if + past … would = imaginary or unlikely now/future.
e: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay in.
If I won a million euros, I'd buy an island.
38.ru: Реальное условие — if + present/will; нереальное — if + past/would.

p: if + past simple / would for imaginary present situations. If I were you … for advice.
I wish + past simple = I'd like things to be different now.
e: If I had more time, I'd learn to cook.
I wish I knew the answer.
39.ru: Нереальное настоящее: if + past, I wish + past.

p: if + had done … would have done = imaginary past (it didn't happen).
I wish + had done = regret about the past.
e: If I'd known, I would have visited you.
I wish I hadn't said that.
40.ru: Нереальное прошлое и сожаления: if/wish + had done.

p: wish + past = now; wish + had done = past; wish + would = you want someone/something to change.
hope is for things that are possible: I hope you have a good time.
e: I wish I could drive.
I wish the bus would come!

p: Passive: be + past participle. We use it when the action matters more than who does it.
is done (present), was done (past). by + person if we need to say who.
e: English is spoken in many countries.
This bridge was built in 1890.
42.ru: Пассив: be + третья форма; важно действие, а не исполнитель.

p: Passive with modals and other forms: will be done, can be done, has been done.
being done for something happening now (is being repaired) and after verbs/prepositions (I hate being told what to do).
e: The results will be announced tomorrow.
The lift is being repaired.
43.ru: Пассив в разных формах: will be done, has been done, is being done.

p: Verbs like give, offer, send, tell can have the person as passive subject: I was given a present.
was/were born; get + past participle for things that happen (get married, get hurt, get paid).
e: She was offered a job.
They got married last summer.
44.ru: I was given/offered…; was born; get + причастие.

p: It is said / believed / thought that … = people say/believe …
Subject + be said / believed / supposed to + verb. be supposed to also = it's planned or the rule.
e: He is said to be very rich.
You're not supposed to park here.
45.ru: Говорят, считается; be supposed to — должно быть / по правилам.

p: have something done = someone else does it for you (have my hair cut).
Also for bad things that happen to you: He had his bike stolen.
e: We're having our car repaired.
She had her bag snatched on the bus.
46.ru: Сделать что-то силами другого человека; также о неприятностях.

p: Reported speech: usually move the verb one step back (is → was, can → could, will → would).
say (something) / tell + person (something).
e: 'I'm tired.' → She said she was tired.
He told me he would call.
47.ru: Косвенная речь: сдвиг времени назад; tell + кому, say + что.

p: Reported questions use normal word order and if/whether for yes/no questions.
Orders and requests: tell / ask + person + (not) to + verb.
e: She asked me where I lived.
Mum told me not to be late.
48.ru: Косвенные вопросы — прямой порядок слов; просьбы — ask/tell + to.

p: Questions: auxiliary + subject + verb (Where do you live?).
If who/what is the subject, no do: Who called? What happened?
e: What time did the film start?
Who ate my sandwich?
49.ru: Вопрос со вспомогательным глаголом; вопрос к подлежащему — без do.

p: Indirect questions (Do you know …? Can you tell me …?) use normal word order.
Don't use do/does/did in them: Do you know where the station is?
e: Could you tell me what time it is?
I don't know why she left.
50.ru: Косвенный вопрос — прямой порядок слов, без do.

p: Short answers and replies use the auxiliary: Yes, I do. / So do I. / Neither can I.
I think so / I hope so / I'm afraid not / I don't think so.
e: 'I love chocolate.' 'So do I.'
'Is it going to rain?' 'I hope not.'
51.ru: Краткие ответы и So do I / Neither am I; I think so / I hope not.

p: Question tags: positive sentence → negative tag, negative sentence → positive tag.
Use the same auxiliary: You live here, don't you? She can't swim, can she?
e: It's cold today, isn't it?
You didn't call him, did you?
52.ru: Разделительные вопросы: + → –, – → +, тот же вспомогательный глагол.

p: Some verbs are followed by -ing: enjoy, finish, mind, avoid, suggest, keep, admit, deny, can't help.
Negative: not + -ing; past: having done.
e: I enjoy cooking for friends.
She denied taking the money.
53.ru: После enjoy, finish, avoid и др. — -ing.

p: Some verbs are followed by to + verb: decide, want, hope, promise, refuse, plan, manage, afford, seem.
Question word + to: I don't know what to do.
e: We decided to take the train.
Can you show me how to use this?
54.ru: После decide, want, hope и др. — to + глагол; what/how to do.

p: Verb + object + to + verb: want, ask, tell, advise, expect, allow + someone to do.
make and let + object + verb without to.
e: I want you to come.
My boss made me work late.
55.ru: want/ask/tell someone to do; make/let someone do (без to).

p: remember/forget doing = a memory of the past; remember/forget to do = a task.
stop doing = finish an activity; stop to do = stop in order to do something. regret doing / regret to tell.
e: Did you remember to lock the door?
We stopped to have a coffee.
56.ru: remember/forget/stop/regret меняют смысл с -ing и с to.

p: try to do = make an effort; try doing = do it as an experiment.
need doing = it needs to be done (The car needs washing). help (to) do; can't help doing.
e: Try restarting your laptop.
The grass needs cutting.
57.ru: try to do — стараться; try doing — попробовать; need doing — нужно сделать.

p: like / love / hate + -ing or to + verb (both OK).
would like / would love / would prefer + to + verb. would like to have done = something you wanted but didn't do.
e: I hate getting up early.
I'd love to visit Japan one day.

p: prefer A to B; prefer doing A to doing B; would prefer to do.
would rather + verb (than + verb); would rather someone did something.
e: I prefer tea to coffee.
I'd rather you didn't smoke in here.
59.ru: prefer … to …; would rather + глагол; would rather you did.

p: After a preposition, use -ing: interested in learning, without saying, before going.
by + -ing = how you do something.
e: She left without saying goodbye.
You can save money by cooking at home.

p: used to do = past habit. be used to doing = it's normal for you. get used to doing = it's becoming normal.
In be/get used to, 'to' is a preposition, so -ing follows.
e: I'm used to getting up early.
It took me months to get used to the noise.
61.ru: used to do — раньше; be/get used to doing — привык(ать) к.

p: Some verbs go with a preposition + -ing: succeed in, insist on, apologise for, accuse of, look forward to, stop from.
verb + object + preposition: thank someone for, blame someone for, congratulate someone on.
e: He apologised for being late.
I'm looking forward to meeting you.
62.ru: Глагол + предлог + -ing: insist on, apologise for, look forward to.

p: It's (not) worth doing / There's no point in doing.
have trouble/difficulty doing; spend/waste time doing; go swimming/shopping/skiing.
e: The museum is worth visiting.
I had difficulty finding the hotel.
63.ru: worth doing, no point in doing, have difficulty doing, go + -ing.

p: to + verb for purpose (why). for + noun for purpose (for some bread).
so that + clause (often with can/could/would).
e: I went to the shop to buy bread.
Speak slowly so that they can understand.
64.ru: Цель: to do, for + существительное, so that + предложение.

p: adjective + to + verb: easy to use, difficult to understand, nice to meet you.
the first/last/only (person) to do something. It's kind of you to …
e: This app is easy to use.
She was the first to arrive.
65.ru: Прилагательное + to: easy to do; the first to do; kind of you to do.

p: afraid to do = you don't do it because it's dangerous; afraid of doing = something might happen by accident.
sorry to (now) / sorry for doing (something you did); interested in doing.
e: I was afraid to touch the dog.
I'm sorry for shouting at you.
66.ru: afraid to do / afraid of doing, sorry to / sorry for — разные смыслы.

p: see/hear somebody do = the whole action; see/hear somebody doing = part of it, in progress.
Same with watch, notice, feel, smell (+ -ing).
e: I saw him cross the road.
I heard someone singing in the shower.
67.ru: see someone do — всё действие; see someone doing — в процессе.

p: -ing clauses can describe two things at the same time or explain why: Feeling tired, I went to bed.
having done = one thing happened before the next.
e: She hurt her back carrying boxes.
Having finished her work, she went home.
68.ru: Причастные обороты с -ing и having done.

p: Countable nouns can be plural and take a/an. Uncountable nouns (advice, information, furniture, news, luggage) have no plural and no a/an.
Use some / a piece of with uncountable nouns.
e: Can I give you some advice?
She's looking for a job (not a work).
69.ru: Исчисляемые и неисчисляемые; advice, information, news — без a и без множественного числа.

p: Some nouns can be countable or uncountable with a different meaning: a coffee / coffee, a hair / hair, a time / time.
Make uncountable nouns countable with a piece of, a bar of, a loaf of, a cup of.
e: I'd like a coffee, please.
Can I have a piece of cake?
70.ru: Одно слово — разные значения; a piece/cup/loaf of — чтобы посчитать.

p: Use a/an with singular countable nouns, especially for jobs and to say what something is.
Use some (or no article) with plurals and uncountable nouns.
e: She's an architect.
I met some nice people.
71.ru: a/an с единственным числом и профессиями; some — с множественным.

p: a/an = one of many, mentioned for the first time. the = we know which one.
the when there is only one in the situation: the door, the station.
e: I saw a film last night. The film was great.
Can you close the door?

p: the for unique things: the sun, the sea, the world, the same, the first, the best.
No article with meals, next/last + time, and usually TV (on TV).
e: We swam in the sea every day.
What did you have for breakfast?
73.ru: the — единственное в своём роде; без артикля — breakfast, next week, on TV.

p: go to school / hospital / prison / university / bed / work for their normal purpose (no the).
the school / the hospital = the building or a specific place.
e: Grandma is in hospital.
I went to the school to see the teacher.
74.ru: school, hospital, bed, work без the — по назначению; с the — здание.

p: No article when talking about things in general: Dogs like bones. Music is important.
the when it's a specific group or thing: The dogs next door bark all night.
e: Exercise is good for you.
The music at the party was too loud.
75.ru: В общем смысле — без артикля; конкретное — с the.

p: the + singular noun for a type of animal or an invention: The giraffe is tall. Who invented the telephone?
the + adjective for groups of people: the rich, the young, the elderly; the + nationality: the French.
e: The tiger is in danger.
The charity helps the homeless.
76.ru: the giraffe — вид в целом; the rich, the French — группа людей.

p: No the with most countries, cities, lakes and single mountains.
the with rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, and countries with Republic/States/Kingdom or plural names.
e: She lives in the United States.
The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
77.ru: Географические названия: страны и города без the, реки, моря, горные цепи — с the.

p: No the with most streets, stations, airports, universities named after places/people: Park Street, Gatwick Airport.
the with hotels, museums, theatres, ships and many newspapers: the Hilton, the British Museum.
e: We stayed at the Ritz.
Our office is on Park Street.
78.ru: Улицы, вокзалы, аэропорты — без the; отели, музеи, театры — с the.

p: Some nouns look plural but are singular: news, physics, maths. Some are always plural: trousers, jeans, glasses, scissors (a pair of …).
police, people are plural. A sum of money/time/distance is singular: Ten miles is a long way.
e: The news is good.
My glasses are broken.
79.ru: news — единственное число; trousers, police — множественное.

p: Noun + noun: the first noun describes the second (a shoe shop, a bus ticket).
The first noun is usually singular: a ten-minute walk, a five-year-old girl.
e: She's a taxi driver.
It's a two-hour flight.
80.ru: Существительное + существительное; первое — обычно в единственном числе.

p: 's for people and animals: my sister's car, the dog's tail. s' for regular plurals: my parents' house.
of for most things: the name of the street, the back of the room. Also today's paper, a week's holiday.
e: That's my parents' house.
What's the name of this street?
81.ru: 's — для людей и животных; of — для предметов.

p: myself / yourself / themselves … when the subject and object are the same person, or to mean 'without help'.
each other = A to B and B to A. Some verbs don't need -self: wash, dress, feel, relax.
e: I taught myself to play the guitar.
They love each other.
82.ru: Возвратные местоимения; each other — друг друга.

p: a friend of mine/yours/his … (not a friend of me).
my own …, a … of my own; on my own / by myself = alone.
e: She's a friend of mine.
He lives on his own.
83.ru: a friend of mine; my own; on my own / by myself — один, сам.

p: there is/are = something exists (first mention). it = something already mentioned, or distance/time/weather.
there will be, there used to be, there must be …
e: There's a new café in our street. It's very nice.
It's ten kilometres to the beach.
84.ru: there is — что-то есть; it — уже упомянутое, расстояние, погода.

p: some in positive sentences and offers; any in negatives and most questions.
something/anybody/anywhere follow the same rule. any can also mean 'it doesn't matter which'.
e: Would you like some cake?
You can sit anywhere you like.
85.ru: some — утверждения и предложения; any — отрицания, вопросы и «любой».

p: no + noun (no tickets); none = not one / not any (none of them).
nobody, nothing, nowhere have a negative meaning — don't use another not with them.
e: There are no tickets left.
I spoke to nobody at the party.
86.ru: no, none, nobody, nothing — уже отрицание, второе not не нужно.

p: much + uncountable, many + plural; a lot of / plenty of with both.
a little / a few = some (positive). little / few = not much / not many (negative).
e: How much money have you got?
He's lonely. He has few friends.
87.ru: much/many; a few/a little — немного; few/little — мало.

p: most / some / all + noun = in general (Most people …).
most of / some of / all of / none of + the/my/these … + noun or pronoun.
e: Most people like music.
Most of my friends live nearby.
88.ru: most people — в общем; most of my friends — из конкретной группы.

p: both = A and B; either = A or B; neither = not A and not B (with a positive verb).
both … and, either … or, neither … nor.
e: Neither answer is correct.
She speaks both German and Russian.
89.ru: both — оба, either — любой из двух, neither — ни один из двух.

p: all + plural/uncountable; every + singular noun; the whole + singular noun.
all day = from morning to night; every day = Monday, Tuesday … everything (not all) = all things.
e: I read the whole book in one night.
I go swimming every day.
90.ru: all, every, whole; all day — весь день, every day — каждый день.

p: each = individually, often a small number (each side of the bed).
every = all of a group, often large; each of / every one of + plural.
e: Each of the children got a present.
I check my email every morning.
91.ru: each — каждый в отдельности; every — все, каждый.

p: Relative clauses tell us which person/thing: who for people, which for things, that for both.
The relative pronoun replaces he/she/it — don't repeat it.
e: The man who lives next door is a pilot.
This is the bus that goes to the airport.
92.ru: Определительные придаточные: who — люди, which — вещи, that — оба.

p: You can leave out who/that/which when it is the object of the clause: the film (that) we saw.
Prepositions often go at the end: the man I was talking to.
e: The cake you made was delicious.
Is this the bag you were looking for?
93.ru: Если that/which — дополнение, его можно опустить; предлог — в конце.

p: whose = possession (the man whose car was stolen). where = place. when = time.
whom = formal object form of who (to whom).
e: That's the house where I was born.
She's the singer whose songs are everywhere.
94.ru: whose — чей, where — где, when — когда, whom — официальное «кого/кому».

p: Extra information clauses add information about someone/something already identified. They have commas.
Use who/which/whose/whom — never that — in these clauses.
e: My brother, who lives in Spain, is a chef.
Paris, which is my favourite city, is expensive.
95.ru: Дополнительная информация — в запятых, без that.

p: most of which / none of whom / both of whom … in extra information clauses.
which can refer to the whole previous sentence: She passed, which surprised everyone.
e: I have ten cousins, most of whom live in Italy.
It rained all day, which meant we stayed in.
96.ru: most of which/whom; which — про всё предыдущее предложение.

p: -ing clauses can replace who is/was doing: the woman talking to Tom.
Past participle clauses replace who was done: the boy injured in the crash.
e: People living here pay a lot of tax.
The money stolen was never found.
97.ru: Причастные обороты вместо придаточных: talking (кто делает), injured (с кем сделали).

p: -ed adjectives describe how you feel (bored, interested, tired).
-ing adjectives describe what causes the feeling (boring, interesting, tiring).
e: I was bored, so I went home.
The film was boring.
98.ru: -ed — как ты себя чувствуешь; -ing — что вызывает чувство.

p: Order of adjectives: opinion, size, age, colour, origin, material: a lovely old Italian house.
After look, feel, sound, taste, smell, seem use an adjective (not an adverb).
e: a big black leather bag
You look tired.

p: Adjectives describe nouns (a careful driver). Adverbs describe verbs, adjectives and other adverbs (drives carefully, really easy).
Most adverbs = adjective + -ly (quick → quickly, happy → happily).
e: She drives carefully.
The test was surprisingly easy.
100.ru: Прилагательное — к существительному, наречие (-ly) — к глаголу.

p: good (adjective) / well (adverb, also = healthy). fast, hard, late are both adjective and adverb.
hardly = almost not; lately = recently. hardly ever / hardly any.
e: She sings well.
I can hardly hear you.
101.ru: good/well; hard — усердно, hardly — едва; late — поздно, lately — недавно.

p: so + adjective/adverb (so tired, so quickly).
such + (a) + adjective + noun (such a nice day, such nice people). so/such … that …
e: It was such a lovely day that we went to the beach.
I'm so tired I could sleep here.

p: too = more than you need/want: too hot to drink.
adjective + enough (old enough); enough + noun (enough money). too/enough + for someone + to do.
e: This bag is too heavy to carry.
We don't have enough chairs.
103.ru: too — слишком; enough — достаточно (после прилагательного, перед существительным).

p: quite, pretty, rather, fairly = less than very. rather often for something negative or surprising.
quite + a/an + adjective + noun (quite a long way). With sure/right/impossible, quite = completely.
e: It's quite a long way.
You're quite right.
104.ru: quite, pretty, rather, fairly — «довольно»; quite right — совершенно верно.

p: Short adjectives add -er (cheaper, bigger); long adjectives use more (more expensive).
Irregular: good → better, bad → worse, far → further/farther. Use than after comparatives.
e: Trains are faster than buses.
This chair is more comfortable.
105.ru: Сравнительная степень: -er или more; good-better, bad-worse.

p: much / a lot / far + comparative = a big difference; a bit / a little / slightly = a small difference.
the … the …: The more you practise, the better you get. Getting colder and colder.
e: I feel much better today.
The more you read, the more you learn.
106.ru: much better, a bit cheaper; the more … the better; colder and colder.

p: as + adjective + as = the same; not as … as = less.
than me / than I am; the same as, similar to, different from.
e: I'm not as tall as my brother.
It's twice as expensive as the other one.
107.ru: as … as — такой же; not as … as — не такой; than me / than I am.

p: Short adjectives: the + -est (the cheapest). Long: the most (the most expensive). good → the best, bad → the worst.
in + place/group (the best in the class); of + number/period (the best of the three). Superlative + I've ever …
e: It's the best book I've ever read.
She's the youngest of the three sisters.
108.ru: Превосходная степень: the -est / the most; in the world, of the three.

p: Don't put words between a verb and its object: I like coffee very much (not like very much coffee).
Usually place before time: She goes to work every day.
e: She speaks English well.
We arrived at the hotel at midnight.
109.ru: Глагол и дополнение не разделяются; место перед временем.

p: Adverbs like always, never, often, also, just, probably go before the main verb …
… but after am/is/are/was/were, and after the first auxiliary (I've never been).
e: I always get up early.
She is often late.
110.ru: always/never/often — перед основным глаголом, но после be и первого вспомогательного.

p: still = something continues. yet = expected, in questions and negatives (at the end).
already = sooner than expected. not … any more / any longer = it has stopped.
e: Is it still raining?
She doesn't live here any more.
111.ru: still — всё ещё; yet — уже/ещё (вопрос, отрицание); already — уже; any more — больше не.

p: even = something surprising (Even my grandmother has a phone).
even + comparative (even colder). even if = whether or not; even though = although (it's true).
e: I'll go even if it rains.
She went to work even though she was ill.
112.ru: even — даже; even if — даже если; even though — хотя (это правда).

p: although / though / even though + clause.
in spite of / despite + noun or -ing (not + clause). despite the rain, despite being ill.
e: Although it was cold, we swam.
Despite the rain, we went out.
113.ru: although + предложение; despite / in spite of + существительное или -ing.

p: in case = because something might happen (do something now to be ready).
in case + present for the future (not will). Different from if (= only when it happens).
e: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
Call me if you need help.
114.ru: in case — на случай, если; if — только если случится.

p: unless = except if / if … not.
as long as / provided (that) = only if. Use the present for the future after them.
e: I won't go unless you come with me.
You can borrow it as long as you bring it back.
115.ru: unless — если не; as long as / provided — при условии, что.

p: as = at the same time as / while: As I was leaving, the phone rang.
as = because: As it was late, we took a taxi.
e: She smiled as she opened the present.
As I don't have a car, I cycle.

p: like + noun/pronoun = similar to (He swims like a fish).
as = in the role of (She works as a nurse), or as + clause (Do it as I showed you).
e: You look like your mother.
I used my coat as a pillow.
117.ru: like — как, похожий на; as — в качестве, так как.

p: as if / as though = it seems that (You look as if you've seen a ghost).
look/sound/feel like + noun/clause (informal: It looks like it's going to rain).
e: He talks as if he knows everything.
It sounds as if they're having fun.
118.ru: as if — как будто; look/sound like — похоже на.

p: during + noun = when (during the film).
for + period = how long (for two hours). while + clause (while I was out).
e: I fell asleep during the film.
She called while I was out.
119.ru: during — во время чего; for — в течение сколько; while — пока (+ предложение).

p: by = not later than (send it by Friday). until = up to that time, continuing (wait until six).
by the time + past perfect / future perfect.
e: Please send it by Friday.
By the time we arrived, the film had started.
120.ru: by — не позже; until — до (продолжаясь); by the time — к тому времени как.

p: at + clock times, night, the weekend, Christmas.
on + days and dates. in + months, years, seasons, parts of the day. No preposition before next, last, this, every.
e: The film starts at 8 o'clock.
I'll see you next week.
121.ru: at — время, on — дни/даты, in — месяцы/годы; без предлога — next, last, every.

p: on time = at the planned time, punctual. in time = early enough (for something / to do something).
at the end (of) = at the final point. in the end = finally, after a long time.
e: The train left on time.
We argued, but in the end we agreed.
122.ru: on time — вовремя (по плану), in time — успеть; at the end of — в конце, in the end — в итоге.

p: in = inside an area or space (in the box, in the room).
at = a point (at the bus stop, at the door). on = a surface (on the table, on the wall).
e: The keys are on the table.
Wait for me at the bus stop.
123.ru: in — внутри, at — в точке, on — на поверхности.

p: Fixed expressions: in a book/magazine/photo, on TV/the radio/a page, at the top/bottom/end of …
on a bus/train/plane, in a car/taxi; at a party/concert, in hospital, at home/work/school.
e: I read it in a magazine.
I left my umbrella on the bus.
124.ru: Устойчивые сочетания с in/at/on: in a magazine, on the bus, at a party.

p: arrive in a town/country; arrive at a building, airport or event (never arrive to).
Use at for places where something happens (at the station, at a concert), in for being inside a building.
e: We arrived in Paris at noon.
They arrived at the airport early.
125.ru: arrive in — город/страна, arrive at — здание/событие; никогда не arrive to.

p: go/come/travel to a place (movement). be at/in a place (position).
into = movement inside (jump into the pool). No to before home: go home.
e: I'm going to the bank.
She jumped into the pool.
126.ru: to — направление, at/in — место, into — движение внутрь; go home без to.

p: Fixed phrases: on holiday, on business, on purpose, on strike, on fire, on foot, on TV.
in cash, in a hurry, in love, in a bad mood, in pencil, in my opinion; at the moment, at first.
e: I did it on purpose.
Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
127.ru: Устойчивые выражения: on purpose, in a hurry, at the moment.

p: by + transport (by car, by train — but on foot), by mistake, by chance, by card.
by = who did it (a song by Adele). with = the tool you use (open it with a knife).
e: We went by train.
He cut the bread with a knife.
128.ru: by — способ/автор; with — инструмент; on foot — пешком.

p: Some nouns take a fixed preposition: reason for, cause of, increase/fall in, answer/solution/invitation to.
relationship with, difference between, demand for, photo of.
e: What's the reason for the delay?
There's been an increase in prices.
129.ru: Существительное + предлог: reason for, cause of, increase in.

p: It's kind/nice/silly of you to …; be kind/nice/rude to someone.
angry with a person / about a thing; excited/worried/upset about; surprised/amazed at/by; fed up with.
e: It was nice of you to help.
I'm worried about my exam.
130.ru: Прилагательное + предлог: kind of you, angry with, worried about.

p: good/bad/terrible at, interested in, afraid/tired/proud/aware/full/capable of, keen on, famous/responsible for.
similar to, married to, used to, different from/to.
e: She's very good at maths.
The room was full of people.
131.ru: Прилагательное + предлог: good at, interested in, afraid of, keen on.

p: listen to, explain something to someone, belong to, reply to, speak/talk to.
look/stare/point/smile/laugh at; shout/throw at (aggressive) vs. throw to (so they catch it).
e: Listen to me!
Why are you staring at me?
132.ru: listen to, explain to; look at, laugh at; throw at / throw to.

p: look for (search), look after (take care of), wait for, ask for, apply for, care for.
talk/ask/hear about; think of/about; discuss + object (no about).
e: I'm looking for my glasses.
Who looks after your kids?
133.ru: look for — искать, look after — присматривать; discuss без about.

p: dream about (in sleep) / dream of (imagine); hear about (news) / hear of (know it exists) / hear from (get a message).
think about (consider) / think of (opinion, idea); remind someone of (similar) / about (don't forget).
e: Have you heard from Tom recently?
This song reminds me of our holiday.
134.ru: about/of/from меняют смысл: hear from, remind of/about, think of/about.

p: accuse of, suffer from, protect from, borrow from, consist of, die of/from.
apologise/blame/punish for; depend/rely/concentrate/spend/congratulate on.
e: It depends on the weather.
She suffers from headaches.
135.ru: Глагол + предлог: depend on, suffer from, accuse of, apologise for.

p: believe in, specialise in, succeed in; crash/bump into, translate into, divide into.
agree with, fill with, provide someone with; happen to, belong to; spend on, insist on.
e: Do you believe in ghosts?
I agree with you.
136.ru: believe in, crash into, agree with, happen to, spend on.

p: A phrasal verb = verb + particle (up, down, out, off …), often with a new meaning: give up, find out.
With a pronoun object, the pronoun goes in the middle: take them off (not take off them).
e: Don't give up!
Put it on.
137.ru: Фразовые глаголы; местоимение ставится между глаголом и частицей.

p: in = into a place / joining: come in, move in, fill in, drop in, fit in.
out = leaving / excluding: go out, move out, drop out, leave out, eat out, check out.
e: Please fill in this form.
We're eating out tonight.

p: out can mean: disappear or stop (go out, run out), solve (work out, sort out), show (point out, turn out), clearly/loudly (speak out).
work out = find the answer / do exercise; turn out = happen in the end.
e: We've run out of coffee.
The party turned out to be great fun.
139.ru: out: закончиться (run out), разобраться (work/sort out), оказаться (turn out).

p: on = connected, working, continuing: turn on, put on, carry on, hold on.
off = disconnected, leaving, cancelled: turn off, take off, set off, call off, go off (alarm, bomb).
e: The plane took off on time.
The match was called off.

p: More on/off: get on with (a person), go on (happen / continue), show off, tell off, put off (postpone), see off.
doze/nod off = fall asleep; drop someone off.
e: I get on well with my colleagues.
Let's put off the meeting until next week.
141.ru: get on with — ладить, put off — откладывать, tell off — отругать, show off — хвастаться.

p: up = higher / increase: stand up, go up, turn up (volume), cheer up, hurry up.
down = lower / decrease / stop: sit down, turn down, calm down, slow down, break down, let down.
e: Can you turn the music down?
The car broke down on the motorway.

p: up = completely or to a new state: give up (stop), take up (start a hobby), grow up, make up (invent), tidy up, wake up.
look up (in a dictionary), turn up (arrive), pick up (collect).
e: She's taken up yoga.
Only five people turned up.
143.ru: give up — бросить, take up — начать, make up — выдумать, turn up — появиться.

p: More with up: bring up (raise a child / mention), set up (start a business), end up (finally be), come up with (an idea).
put up with (tolerate), keep up with (go at the same speed).
e: She set up her own company.
I can't put up with this noise.
144.ru: bring up, set up, end up, come up with, put up with, keep up with.

p: away = leaving, not here, getting rid of: go away, run away, throw away, give away, put away, keep away.
back = returning: come back, call back, pay back, give back, take back, look back.
e: Don't throw that away.
I'll call you back in five minutes.
